title: The Horizon of New Lagos Anew
premise: Astrid Delacroix tends the Verdance, a generational garden ship orbiting dead Mars, growing forests for descendants of two human factions—the Earthbound and the Diaspora—who severed contact a century ago after the Schism War. When gravity stutters across the system for nine seconds, the Verdance's reactor begins an irreversible countdown that will either wake one cryosleep archive or the other, but not both. Astrid, who secretly loves Imani Okonkwo, a courier running the forbidden route between the estranged worlds, must choose which half of humanity wakes—and discovers the nine-second flicker was a message from the garden's original designers, proving both archives were always meant to live. In the end, Astrid reroutes the reactor through the garden's living root-system, waking both archives at half-strength, and she and Imani plant the first orchard of the reunited worlds.
about_author: Wren Thackeray is a former hydrologist who spent six years aboard research vessels in the Southern Ocean before turning to fiction, and whose work is known for botany rendered with liturgical reverence. They live in Lisbon with a partner and an unreasonable number of ferns.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, tending the Verdance's orchards when gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, dropping every leaf and every heart. The reactor wakes with a countdown no one authorized. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine, the garden suddenly listening back.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Imani's POV, running a courier run between Earth and the Diaspora stations, smuggling letters between families split by the Schism. She hears the gravity-flicker hit both worlds at once. Emotional beat: loneliness transmuted into purpose; two worlds that won't speak, speaking through her.

chapters.title: Archive A, Archive B
chapters.summary: Astrid and the Verdance council learn the countdown's terms: enough power to wake either the Earthborn archive or the Diaspora archive, not both. Astrid's own mother sleeps in Archive B. Emotional beat: the horror of a binary choice dressed as engineering.

chapters.title: Letters in the Hull
chapters.summary: Imani docks at the Verdance, delivering contraband letters, including one addressed to Astrid from her mother, written before cryosleep. First meeting in years; old love rekindles in a cargo bay. Emotional beat: tenderness as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The garden's oldest trees predate the Schism; their root-network carries data from the original designers. Astrid finds a fragment: the flicker was a signal, not an accident. Emotional beat: wonder, and the sense of being watched by the dead.

chapters.title: Council of the Unborn
chapters.summary: The council debates waking one archive; factions form along old Earthbound/Diaspora lines even aboard the neutral Verdance. Astrid stays silent about the signal fragment. Emotional beat: complicity and the cost of withholding truth for the right reasons.

chapters.title: The Courier's Debt
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Earth authorities intercept her manifest and demand she carry an ultimatum to the Verdance: wake Archive A or lose all supply lines. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a noose around the person she loves.

chapters.title: Rootspeak
chapters.summary: Astrid decodes more of the root-network with the garden's blind archivist, Teodoro. The designers' message: the flicker was a test of whether humanity could choose both. The countdown is the exam. Emotional beat: hope that feels like heresy.

chapters.title: Half a Humanity
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, walking the cryo-bays, reading the names in both archives—her mother in one, Imani's brother in the other. Emotional beat: grief made specific; the abstract choice becomes faces.

chapters.title: The Ultimatum Arrives
chapters.summary: Imani delivers Earth's ultimatum publicly; the council fractures, and a faction led by Councilor Vasquez begins manually arming Archive A's wake sequence. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing the mask of pragmatism.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Orchards
chapters.summary: Someone floods the root-lab to destroy the decoded signal. Astrid suspects Vasquez; Imani suspects everyone. Emotional beat: paranoia poisoning a community built on patience.

chapters.title: What Imani Carried
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. She confesses she has been carrying more than letters—she holds a Diaspora key that could interface with the reactor, given to her by her brother before his cryosleep. Emotional beat: the relief and terror of a shared secret.

chapters.title: The Countdown Accelerates
chapters.summary: Vasquez's tampering destabilizes the reactor; the countdown drops from months to weeks. Both archives now risk dying unwoken. Emotional beat: the binary collapsing into something worse—total loss.

chapters.title: Negotiation with the Earthbound
chapters.summary: Astrid broadcasts the designers' message to both worlds, asking for trust. Earth answers with silence; the Diaspora answers with a single word: begin. Emotional beat: the ache of loving people who refuse to be reasonable.

chapters.title: Teodoro's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: The archivist reveals the root-network can carry reactor load—but only if the garden's oldest trees are sacrificed, the very forest Astrid has tended for twenty years. Emotional beat: inheritance means being willing to spend what you were given.

chapters.title: Vasquez's Reason
chapters.summary: Astrid confronts Vasquez, who confesses the sabotage: her entire family sleeps in Archive A, and she could not bear the arithmetic. Emotional beat: enemy revealed as mirror; mercy as strategy and as grace.

chapters.title: The Route Reopened
chapters.summary: Imani flies the forbidden route one last time, carrying Vasquez's surrender and Astrid's plan to both worlds, forcing Earth and Diaspora to respond to the same document for the first time in a century. Emotional beat: courage as a courier's craft.

chapters.title: Felling the First Forest
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The crew begins cutting the ancient trees to wire their roots into the reactor. Astrid makes the first cut herself. Emotional beat: mourning and purpose fused; a garden becoming a bridge.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds Again
chapters.summary: The climax: as the countdown hits zero, gravity flickers again—nine seconds in which the root-network must hold both wake sequences. Imani holds the key-interface, Vasquez holds the reactor steady, Astrid holds the living circuit. Emotional beat: everything held at once, by everyone, together.

chapters.title: Both Archives Wake
chapters.summary: Both archives stir at half-strength—weak, slow, alive. Astrid's mother opens her eyes; Imani's brother coughs a century out of his lungs. Emotional beat: the impossible arithmetic solved by refusal, and the trembling after.

chapters.title: The First Orchard
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Earth and Diaspora ships arrive at the Verdance together. Astrid and Imani plant the first orchard from cuttings of the felled ancients, both delegations planting alongside. Emotional beat: reconciliation as cultivation, not declaration.

chapters.title: The Horizon of New Lagos Anew
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, years on: New Lagos, the first joint settlement, at sunrise; her mother teaching children to graft, Imani's routes now official. The garden's new trees are tall enough to whisper. Emotional beat: belonging as something grown, inherited, and handed on.
